steps.title: to be · present
steps.html:
PersonPositiveNegativeQuestion
II am / I'm Turkish.I'm not Turkish.Am I late?
He / She / ItShe is / She's French.She isn't French.Is she French?
You / We / TheyThey are / They're British.They aren't British.Are they British?

In speech people almost always use the short form: I'm, she's, they're.

For a question, put am / is / are before the person.

Short answers: Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.

The past of these is was and were, from Lesson 1.

steps.title: Plural nouns
steps.html:
The noun ends in…RuleExample
most nounsadd -sname → names
-s, -ch, -sh, -xadd -eslanguage → languages, church → churches
consonant + -y-y becomes -iescountry → countries
irregularlearn themman → men, woman → women, person → people, child → children

steps.title: Shakira
steps.html: Shakira is a singer from Colombia. She is Colombian, but her grandparents are from Lebanon. Spanish is her first language, but she speaks four languages: Spanish, English, Portuguese and some Arabic. English is very important for her, because she is a big star in the USA, Spain and Brazil. Millions of people are fans of her songs.

steps.title: Son Heung-min
steps.html: Son Heung-min is a footballer from South Korea. He isn't Chinese or Japanese – he is Korean. His first big club was in Germany. He was only sixteen, so his German is very good. Later he was a star in London for ten years. His teammates are men from many different countries, so English is important for him too. His fans are people of all ages: men, women and children.
